about: A third-person novel with one first-person letter set in its first chapter: the model may quote a line of the letter as the narrator's, but the narration outside the letter is third person and the code reads it so.
title: The Thursday Post
author: Gerda Lindqvist-Roe

chapters.title: Thursday
paragraphs: The post came up the valley on Thursdays, and Edda Marrow was waiting at the gate before the cart had cleared the bridge.
She had waited at that gate every Thursday since March. The carter knew it and always slowed his horse.
This time he held out a single envelope, grey with road dust. Edda turned it over twice before she opened it.
Inside was a letter in her brother's hand. She sat down on the stone step to read it.

Dear Edda, I write from the harbour town, where I have found work at last. I did not tell you before because I was afraid you would worry. I will send money at the end of the month, and I will come home when the snow melts. Your brother, Anton.
Edda read it a third time. Then she folded it along its creases and put it into her apron.
Pavel came across the yard with a bucket in each hand. He set them down and looked at her face.
"None at all," Edda said. "Anton has found work."
He picked up the buckets again. He did not say that Anton had left in the autumn without a word, and that nobody had expected a letter.
The kitchen was warm and smelled of bread. Edda put the kettle on the hob and set two cups on the table.
Pavel drank his tea standing, the way he always did. He watched the lane through the small window above the sink.
The sun moved across the floor. The clock on the dresser struck eleven and then, after a pause, struck once more by mistake.
Edda took down the tin where she kept the household money. She counted it twice and wrote the sum on the back of an old bill.
In the afternoon she walked down to the bridge. The river was high with meltwater and the planks were wet underfoot.
Edda stood there until the light began to go. Then she turned back toward the farm, where Pavel had already lit the lamp.
